title: Signature Requirement Synthesis Record

Overview

This record belongs to the Cross-Disciplinary Design Synthesis Signature Database (Signature edition), Manon's original counterpart to the public database of the same name. Requirement Synthesis Record covers the following in Signature terms: gathers requirements from all disciplines into one structured set. The record is written as a complete, usable file, with a demo program genuinely executed at build time and its output stored beside the code. Design targets only: labels in this record describe design targets for engineering work, never a claim of NASA, DARPA, or contractor qualification or approval.

How the Signature design works

The Signature design works like this: a synthesis record gathers requirements and constraints from every involved discipline into one matrix, scores trade options against all of them at once, and records conflicts with their resolutions, so no discipline's constraint is silently dropped. Applied to this record, the design means the following in practice: gathers requirements from all disciplines into one structured set. The record sits at ladder rank simple in the teaching ladder, which runs simple, then compounded, then most complex, so a Signature reader can start from the simpler records and work toward this one.

Worked example

The demo scores design options across disciplines and prints the best option under stated weights. The demo program prints:

Option scores: [('Option A', 70), ('Option B', 65), ('Option C', 60)]

Use and limits

A synthesized design is a design, not a built system. Its scores compare options under stated weights, and changing the weights can change the ranking, which the record must show.
